title: Great American Artificial Intelligence Act
sponsor: Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA); Rep. Lori Trahan (D-MA)
summary: Bipartisan 269-page discussion draft that would establish a national AI policy framework and preempt state laws specifically regulating AI model development for three years. Preemption does not apply to laws on AI deployment or use. The bill also creates voluntary federal oversight processes for frontier AI models. Opposed by consumer groups; supported by tech industry.
robotics_scope: Preempts state regulations on AI model development, including robotics foundation models; shapes national framework for AI-enabled autonomous systems

title: Executive Order: Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security
summary: Directs federal agencies to create a voluntary 30-day pre-release review framework for frontier AI models, establish an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, and develop benchmarks assessing AI cyber capabilities. Narrowed from an initial 90-day mandatory window after industry objections. Covers AI foundation models used in autonomous robots and humanoids.
robotics_scope: AI foundation models powering autonomous robots and humanoid systems subject to voluntary pre-release review

title: Robots For America Coalition Policy Framework
summary: Robots For America is a private industry coalition that released a federal policy agenda in May 2026 on deployment finance, tax, regulation, workforce, and logistics. It is not a government order or enacted policy.
robotics_scope: Non-government proposals aimed at federal robotics policy; included as stakeholder context.

title: DOE Genesis Mission
summary: The Genesis Mission, launched in November 2025, links DOE national laboratories, scientific data, AI, and experimental platforms. DOE launched a consortium in February 2026; robotics and automation are among relevant enabling technologies. The program is broader than the earlier dashboard description of 14 robotics projects.
robotics_scope: Autonomous science, laboratory automation, and robotics relevant to DOE research missions.

title: DOE Exascale Foundry
sponsor: Oak Ridge National Laboratory + Autonomous Resource Corp
summary: Public-private partnership to accelerate AI-enabled defense manufacturing using national lab supercomputing capabilities and autonomous fabrication tools.
robotics_scope: AI-enabled defense manufacturing

title: American Security Robotics Act of 2026
summary: Restricts federal procurement of humanoid robots and robotic systems manufactured in countries of concern (notably China), citing supply-chain security and dual-use concerns. Establishes a covered-entity list maintained by Commerce and DoD.
robotics_scope: Federal procurement restrictions on foreign-made robots

title: Special Conditions: Skyryse, Robinson Helicopter Company Model R66 Helicopter; Flight Control System Annunciation of Control
summary: This action proposes special conditions for the Robinson Helicopter Company (Robinson) Model R66 helicopter. This helicopter, as modified by Skyryse, will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for normal category helicopters. This design feature replaces the mechanical flight controls with a digital fly-by-wire (FBW) system. The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.
robotics_scope: FAA special conditions for Skyryse’s automated flight-control retrofit of the Robinson R66

title: Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for Exemption From Aurora Operations, Inc.
sponsor: Transportation Department, Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
summary: FMCSA requests public comment on Aurora Operations, Inc.'s (Aurora) application for a five-year exemption to allow commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) equipped with a Level 4 automated driving system (ADS) to use a set of cab-mounted warning beacons in lieu of placing reflective warning triangles or fusees around the stopped vehicle. The exemption would apply to Aurora and to other motor carriers operating Level 4 ADS-equipped CMVs that notify FMCSA in writing prior to operating under the exemption. FMCSA is required by statute to publish a notice explaining each exemption request, and such notice does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach on the request. After reviewing the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted, FMCSA will grant or deny the exemption.
robotics_scope: FMCSA exemption request from Aurora to run driverless commercial trucks without physical warning devices

title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 110 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
sponsor: Transportation Department, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
summary: NHTSA is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 110, "Tire selection and rims and motor home/ recreation vehicle trailer load carrying capacity information for motor vehicles with a GVWR of 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds) or less." The proposed modification would amend a single section of the standard to enable compliance by affixing the required placard on the left side of the vehicle when there is not a "driver's side" for vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls. This rulemaking would allow flexibility in complying with the standard without detriment to vehicle safety. This action is part of a larger NHTSA effort to address vehicle automation in the agency's regulations.
robotics_scope: NHTSA rulemaking adapting tire and rim safety standards to vehicles with no human driver

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Notice and Request for Comment; Novel Human-Machine Interface (HMI) Designs
sponsor: Transportation Department, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
summary: NHTSA invites public comments about the agency's intention to request approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for a new information collection. Before a Federal agency can collect certain information from the public, it must receive approval from OMB. Under procedures established by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, before seeking OMB approval, Federal agencies must solicit public comment on proposed collections of information, including extensions and reinstatement of previously approved collections. This document describes a collection of information request, titled "Novel Human- Machine Interface (HMI) Designs", for which NHTSA intends to seek OMB approval to conduct a one-time study.
robotics_scope: NHTSA information collection on novel human-machine interfaces in automated vehicles

title: Initiation of Section 301 Investigations: Acts, Policies, and Practices of Certain Economies Relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors
sponsor: Trade Representative, Office of United States
summary: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) has initiated investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 regarding the acts, policies, and practices of certain economies relating to structural excess capacity and production in certain manufacturing sectors. Key trading partners have developed production capacity untethered from the incentives of domestic and global demand. This excess capacity leads to, among others, overproduction and large or persistent trade surpluses, as well as underutilized and unused capacity, in manufacturing sectors. These investigations will focus on economies that appear to exhibit structural excess capacity and production in various manufacturing sectors, such as through large or persistent trade surpluses or underutilized or unused
robotics_scope: USTR Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity — the mechanism behind China’s manufacturing scale

title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 103 and FMVSS No. 104 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles; Incorporation by Reference
sponsor: Transportation Department, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
summary: NHTSA is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) No. 103, "Windshield defrosting and defogging systems," and FMVSS No. 104, "Windshield wiping and washing systems." The proposed modifications would except vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls from these standards. This rulemaking would remove unnecessary regulatory burdens and costs associated with systems intended to provide visibility for a person driving the vehicle. As these systems do not fulfill the same safety need on an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls, the proposed changes are not expected to have adverse safety effects. Manufacturers may still provide these systems if they choose to do so. These actions ar
robotics_scope: NHTSA rulemaking adapting windshield defrost and wiper standards to ADS-equipped vehicles

title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 102 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
sponsor: Transportation Department, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
summary: NHTSA is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 102, "Transmission shift position sequence, starter interlock, and transmission braking effect." The proposed modification would except vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls from the requirement for a transmission shift position display. This rulemaking would remove unnecessary regulatory burdens and costs associated with a display designed to aid a person driving the vehicle. As the transmission shift position display does not fulfill the same safety need in an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls, the amendment will not impact vehicle safety. This action is part of a larger NHTSA effort to address vehicle automation
robotics_scope: NHTSA rulemaking adapting transmission shift and starter-interlock standards to ADS-equipped vehicles

title: Space Force Otter Spacecraft Contract
summary: A $54.5M procurement contract awarded to Starfish Space for their Otter spacecraft to perform on-orbit satellite servicing and refueling.
robotics_scope: On-orbit satellite servicing spacecraft

title: National Commission on Robotics Act
summary: Directs the Department of Commerce to establish an independent National Commission on Robotics composed of 18 recognized robotics experts, appointed by Congressional leadership and the President. The Commission would submit an interim report within one year and a final report with actionable recommendations on U.S. robotics competitiveness within two years.
robotics_scope: National robotics strategy and coordination

title: Space Force On-Orbit Satellite Servicing Missions
summary: Initiative to launch 4 satellite servicing, refueling, and inspection missions in 2026 in partnership with AFRL and DARPA: DARPA RSGS, Astroscale refueler, Tetra-5 (with AFRL), and Starfish Otter.
robotics_scope: Satellite servicing and refueling autonomy

title: Section 174 R&D Expensing
summary: Restores full first-year deduction for domestic R&D expenses (foreign R&D still amortized over 15 years), reversing the amortization requirement. Provides material cash-flow relief for pre-revenue robotics startups whose payroll is the bulk of Qualified Research Expenses.
robotics_scope: Tax treatment of domestic research & development payroll and expenses

title: 100% bonus depreciation under Public Law 119-21
summary: Permanent 100% additional first-year depreciation is available for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025. Eligible machinery and equipment may qualify; treatment depends on the asset and taxpayer. This is an enacted tax provision, not a robotics-only credit.
robotics_scope: Potential first-year deduction for eligible purchased automation equipment; asset-specific tax rules apply.

title: NIST Humanoid Robot Baseline Performance Benchmark
summary: NIST is developing baseline humanoid performance benchmarks, test apparatus, and protocols for mobility and manipulation. The public project page describes planned work; it does not establish a completed certification standard.
robotics_scope: Humanoid performance metrics and baseline standards

title: Adjusting Imports of Semiconductors, Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment, and Their Derivative Products Into the United States
summary: Federal Register Presidential Document: Adjusting Imports of Semiconductors, Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment, and Their Derivative Products Into the United States
robotics_scope: Section 232 action on semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment — the upstream inputs robots are built from

title: DARPA Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS)
summary: Program developing a robotic servicing vehicle equipped with NRL-built robotic arms to repair, inspect, and upgrade satellites in geosynchronous orbit, scheduled for a 2026 launch.
robotics_scope: Space robotics, manipulator autonomy

title: Hazardous Materials: Modernizing Regulations To Facilitate Transportation of Hazardous Materials Using Highly Automated Transportation Systems
sponsor: Transportation Department, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration
summary: The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) is publishing this advance notice of proposed rulemaking (ANPRM) to obtain stakeholder input on potential revisions to the Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) to facilitate the safe transportation of hazardous materials using highly automated transportation systems.
robotics_scope: PHMSA advance rulemaking on moving hazardous materials with highly automated transportation systems

title: Commerce Section 232 investigation — robotics and industrial machinery imports
summary: The Commerce Department initiated a national-security investigation into imports of robotics and industrial machinery in September 2025 and sought public comments. BIS still lists it as an investigation; this record does not indicate a final tariff or finding.
robotics_scope: Potential import-policy exposure for robotics and industrial machinery; product coverage and outcome remain unresolved.

title: NIST SP 1227 (Draft) — Performance Metrics for Robotic Assembly & Manipulation
summary: Draft special publication outlining performance metrics and test methods for robotic assembly and manipulation in manufacturing environments.
robotics_scope: Robotic assembly standards

title: Additions and Revisions to the Entity List
sponsor: Commerce Department, Industry and Security Bureau
summary: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 32 entities to the Entity List. These entries are listed on the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China) (23), India, (1), Iran (1), Singapore (1), Taiwan (1), Turkey (3), and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) (2). These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States. This final rule revises an entry by removing two addresses from one entity under the destination of Russia. Finally, this rule amends 27 existing entries on the Entity List to correct typographical errors under the following destinations: Belarus (3), China (11), Iran (1), Pakistan
robotics_scope: BIS adds 32 China-based entities to the Entity List, restricting export of robotics-relevant technology

title: ARPA-E — Embodied AI for Energy Systems Solicitation
summary: ARPA-E open program-area solicitation targeting embodied AI applied to energy infrastructure: grid inspection, fuel-cycle maintenance, wind/solar plant operations. Typical awards $1–10M. Robotics startups partnering with utilities + national labs are competitive.
robotics_scope: Robotics + AI for energy infrastructure

title: America's AI Action Plan
sponsor: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy
summary: July 2025 White House plan organizes AI policy across innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security. It addresses open models, adoption, manufacturing, workers, science datasets, evaluations, government use, exports, and cybersecurity; it is not a stand-alone robotics plan.
robotics_scope: Directly relevant sections include manufacturing, open models, scientific datasets, evaluations, worker training, adoption, and secure exports.

title: Notice of Request for Information (RFI) on Autonomous Experimentation Platforms from Material Genome Initiative
summary: On behalf of the Material Genome Initiative (MGI), the Department of Energy (DOE) seeks public comment on autonomous experimentation platforms to inform implementation of the MGI Challenges and Autonomous Materials Innovation Infrastructure (AMII).
robotics_scope: Federal Register publication

title: EDA Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (Robotics Clusters)
summary: Regional hubs designation and funding, including robotics-anchored advanced manufacturing clusters, designed to build regional technology ecosystems across the U.S.
robotics_scope: Regional robotics clusters

title: DoD Replicator Initiative
summary: Pentagon initiative to field thousands of attritable autonomous systems (air, sea, ground) within 18–24 months, with subsequent tranches expanding scope. Drives near-term procurement of robotics from non-traditional suppliers including startups.
robotics_scope: Mass-deployable autonomous defense systems

title: California — CPUC Autonomous Vehicle Passenger Service Programs
summary: Under its AV passenger-service framework, the CPUC issues Drivered/Driverless Pilot and Deployment permits that let companies such as Waymo carry passengers for a fare in autonomous vehicles. On Aug. 10, 2023 the Commission approved resolutions allowing fared, driverless robotaxi operation 24/7 in San Francisco, and in Aug. 2025 opened rulemaking R.25-08-013 to update AV passenger-transport rules. Operators must also hold a parallel California DMV deployment permit.
robotics_scope: Robotaxi/AV passenger-service permitting & oversight

title: Texas — Texas Enterprise Fund
sponsor: Office of the Governor, Texas Economic Development
summary: Performance-based deal-closing cash grants for a new or expanding Texas site competing with an out-of-state location. The project must exceed 75 new full-time jobs in urban areas or 25 in rural areas, meet wage and capital-investment tests, and show local support. This is not a robotics-specific franchise-tax credit.
robotics_scope: Potential support for qualifying robotics manufacturing or deployment facilities; substantial jobs and investment thresholds apply.

title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
summary: Voluntary framework providing guidance for managing risks in AI systems, including embodied AI and robotics applications. Sets out core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Increasingly cited by procurement agencies as a baseline for AI-enabled robot systems.
robotics_scope: AI / autonomy safety standards

title: Michigan — Research and Development Tax Credit
summary: Michigan provides a refundable R&D tax credit for qualifying research expenses incurred in the state beginning with tax years after January 1, 2025. It is broad rather than restricted to mobility or robotics; annual claim and proration rules apply.
robotics_scope: Qualifying Michigan robotics R&D expenditures may be eligible under the general credit.

title: Pennsylvania — Innovate in PA 2.0
sponsor: PA Department of Community and Economic Development
summary: The signed FY2026–27 budget provides $125 million to create Innovate in PA 2.0. DCED describes venture-capital access, research commercialization, and regional innovation ecosystems, with robotics among named sectors. It is not a Pittsburgh-only tax abatement or a Pittsburgh Robotics Network membership benefit.
robotics_scope: Broad innovation-capital and commercialization support with robotics named as a sector.
beneficiaries: Pennsylvania innovation ecosystem and eligible firms

title: CHIPS and Science Act — Advanced Manufacturing Provisions
summary: Allocates $52.7B for semiconductor manufacturing and authorizes additional R&D programs at NSF, NIST, and DoE — including advanced manufacturing and robotics R&D. Manufacturing USA institutes (including the Advanced Robotics Manufacturing Institute / ARM) received substantial new authorizations.
robotics_scope: Advanced manufacturing R&D, Manufacturing USA institutes

title: USDA/NSF Agricultural Robotics Partnership
summary: Partnership between NIFA and NSF to fund collaborative proposals for agricultural robotics innovation under the National Robotics Initiative framework.
robotics_scope: Collaborative agricultural robotics

title: North Carolina — Advanced Manufacturing Job Development Grant
summary: Discretionary grant program for major advanced-manufacturing investments. Has been used by automotive and robotics OEMs; payouts based on jobs created, capex, and wage levels relative to county average.
robotics_scope: Major manufacturing investment

title: NSF National Robotics Initiative 3.0
summary: Multi-agency funding program for fundamental research in integrative robotics, especially co-robots that interact with humans. Awards $500K–$1.5M typical grant size, with $50M+ annual budget. Open to academic + industry partnerships.
robotics_scope: Robotics R&D — human-robot interaction, integrative systems

title: NIH NIBIB Bioengineering Research Grants (Robotics)
summary: Funding track supporting bioengineering research and SBIR/STTR grants for surgical, assistive, and rehabilitation robotics.
robotics_scope: Medical, assistive, and surgical robotics

title: DOT Automated Vehicle and UAS Safety Oversight
summary: Safety frameworks, testing guidelines, and airspace/on-road operational authorizations for autonomous vehicles and commercial unmanned aircraft systems (drones).
robotics_scope: Autonomous vehicles and UAS regulatory framework

title: NSF Foundational Research in Robotics (FRR)
summary: A joint program across NSF directorates supporting foundational and academic research in robotics, spanning manipulation, locomotion, sensing, and human-robot interaction.
robotics_scope: Foundational academic robotics research

title: USDA/NSF Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes (Agriculture Track)
summary: Jointly funded AI institutes focusing on agriculture, including AgAID (for agricultural workforce and specialty crops) and AIFARMS (focusing on livestock and soil health).
robotics_scope: AI and robotics in agriculture

title: New York — Excelsior Jobs Program
summary: Empire State Development offers job, investment, and R&D tax credits to qualifying firms in listed strategic industries. Manufacturing, scientific R&D, and software firms generally need at least five net new jobs; there is no separate robotics or AI track.
robotics_scope: Robotics firms may qualify through manufacturing, scientific R&D, or software eligibility and job thresholds.

title: Florida — HB 311 (Autonomous Vehicles)
summary: CS/HB 311, effective July 1, 2019, authorizes a fully autonomous vehicle to operate on Florida roads regardless of whether a human operator is physically present, and provides that a licensed human operator is not required. It deems the automated driving system to be the legal operator while engaged, and sets insurance requirements for on-demand autonomous-vehicle networks. The law makes Florida one of the most permissive states for fully driverless operation and deployment.
robotics_scope: Fully driverless AV operation & deployment

title: Arizona — Executive Order 2018-04 (Autonomous Vehicle Testing & Operating)
summary: Executive Order 2018-04 updated Arizona's framework for testing and operating autonomous vehicles, requiring driverless operators to comply with NHTSA voluntary safety standards and to register fully driverless vehicles with the state, and to bring a vehicle to a 'minimal risk condition' if the automated system fails. The order made Arizona an early hub for fully driverless operation — home to Waymo's commercial robotaxi service — alongside testing by GM, Uber, and Intel.
robotics_scope: Driverless AV testing & deployment rules

title: California — California Competes Tax Credit (GO-Biz)
sponsor: Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)
summary: Competitive tax credit for businesses expanding or relocating in California, assessed on jobs, investment, and other statutory factors. It is sector-neutral. GO-Biz lists FY2026–27 application windows of July 20–August 10, 2026; January 4–25, 2027; and March 1–15, 2027.
robotics_scope: Advanced-manufacturing & R&D job/investment tax credits

title: Nevada — AB 511 / NRS Chapter 482A (Autonomous Vehicles)
sponsor: Nevada State Legislature (signed by Gov. Brian Sandoval)
summary: Signed in June 2011, AB 511 made Nevada the first U.S. state to authorize autonomous vehicles on public highways and directed the DMV to adopt operating and testing regulations, now codified in NRS Chapter 482A. It defines an autonomous vehicle as one using AI, sensors, and GPS to drive without active human intervention, and requires manufacturers/developers to self-certify compliance and register before operating. The statute established the licensing and insurance/bond foundation for AV testing in the state.
robotics_scope: AV testing & deployment licensing statute

title: Research and Development Tax Credit
summary: Permanent tax credit on qualified research expenses (QREs) including employee wages, supplies, cloud computing, and contractor fees. Routinely claimed by robotics companies for prototype builds, control-system R&D, and manufacturing process optimization.
robotics_scope: Tax credit for qualified research activities

title: FCC Covered List expansion — advanced robotic devices and connected power inverters
summary: On July 28, 2026 the FCC added foreign-produced advanced robotic devices to its Covered List, with an exception for devices receiving Department of War conditional approval. The September 18 FCC notice announced conditional approvals and exemptions for certain devices. The restriction concerns new equipment authorization; current authorization and device scope require case-specific review.
robotics_scope: Network-capable foreign-produced advanced robotic devices; DoW conditional approval and FCC equipment-authorization process matter.

title: GUARD Act of 2026 — Guarding the U.S. against Adversarial Robotics Dominance
sponsor: Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) and Rep. Jennifer McClellan (D-VA)
summary: Would require national security agencies to review humanoid and quadruped robots produced in China and other foreign adversary countries, and add platforms judged an unacceptable national security risk to the FCC's Covered List — barring their sale in the US. Any platform not reviewed within one year would be added automatically. Extends to robotics the Covered List machinery already applied to telecom equipment and drones. Introduced in the 119th Congress; on September 1, 2026, the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology marked up the bill and forwarded it to the full Committee by voice vote. The related provision that advanced in the House-passed FY2027 NDAA is Section 163, passed 216-212 on July 22, 2026: it bars the Department of Defense (not the wider federal government) from procuring, leasing, or operating a "covered humanoid robotic system" produced or developed by China (or incorporating Chinese firmware, software, AI models, cloud services, or remote-access/update capability); industrial robots, non-networked systems, and regulated medical devices are expressly excluded from the definition. Commercial sales remain legal under the NDAA provision — the GUARD Act's broader Covered List approach would go further.
robotics_scope: Robotics is the entire subject of the bill: it defines a review-and-list regime specifically for foreign-adversary humanoid and quadruped robots.

title: Seeking Comment on Prohibiting the Importation and Marketing of Certain Covered UAS and UAS Critical Components and Equipment Listed in Section 1709 of FY2025 NDAA.
summary: In this document, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (PSHSB) and the Office of Engineering and Technology (OET) seek comment on proposing to prohibit the continued importation and marketing of certain previously authorized equipment that has been determined to pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or to the and security of United States persons. Through Public Notice, acting pursuant to section 2.939 of the Federal Communications Commission's rules, PSHSB and OET propose to apply such prohibitions to certain previously-authorized foreign-produced uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS) and UAS critical components, and certain communications and video surveillance equipment listed in section 1709 of the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 (FY2025 NDAA), added to the Covered List in December 2025.
robotics_scope: Federal Register publication

title: Medical Devices; Ear, Nose, and Throat Devices; Classification of the Cooperative Powered Surgical Assist Device for ENT Surgery
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the cooperative powered surgical assist device for ear, nose, and throat (ENT) surgery into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the cooperative powered surgical assist device for ENT surgery. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.
robotics_scope: FDA classifies the cooperative powered surgical assist device for ENT surgery into Class II — a regulatory pathway for robotic-assisted surgical tools.

title: Presidential Proclamation adjusts Section 232 tariffs on drone imports — up to 100%, effective Sept. 3, 2026
summary: President Trump signed a proclamation on August 13, 2026 imposing Section 232 tariffs on imported unmanned aircraft systems (UAS/drones) and components, following a national-security investigation into import dependence. Tariffs took effect September 3, 2026: 100% on higher-risk UAS (over 25kg or with thermal-imaging capability) and related equipment, 25% on other covered UAS, with reduced rates for qualifying imports from the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan, Liechtenstein and the UK, and a 180-day delayed implementation for certain less-sensitive components. The broader Section 232 investigation into robotics and industrial machinery imports (separate from drones) remains open as of mid-September 2026.
robotics_scope: Drones (UAS) are a robotics category tracked by this site; the tariff directly restricts imports of foreign-made drone hardware and components on national-security grounds, and is procedurally linked to the still-open Section 232 robotics/industrial-machinery investigation (fedreg-2025-18749).

title: FY2026 NDAA Section 225 — Army directed to expand robotic automation in munitions manufacturing
summary: The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, signed into law December 18, 2025, authorizes over $25B to rebuild the U.S. munitions arsenal. Section 225 specifically directs the Army to expand robotic automation in ammunition/munitions manufacturing to improve safety, output and workforce training, with coordination through Army program offices.
robotics_scope: Directly mandates expansion of robotic automation within a specific, funded federal manufacturing base (munitions/ammunition production).

title: Chip EQUIP Act (H.R. 6207) — bars foreign-adversary semiconductor manufacturing equipment purchases
sponsor: Rep. Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) and Rep. Erin Houchin (R-IN)
summary: The Chip Equipment Quality, Usefulness, and Integrity Protection Act ("Chip EQUIP Act") would prohibit purchases of certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment from foreign entities of concern or their subsidiaries. Referred to the House Committees on Energy and Commerce and on Science, Space, and Technology; reported out of the full House Energy & Commerce Committee by a 39-0 roll call vote on September 16, 2026, alongside the GUARD Act in the same markup window — a companion bill, S. 3301, carries the same name in the Senate. Extends the chip/equipment export-control logic already central to the US-China tech contest explicitly into the equipment that manufactures semiconductors, which in turn are the compute layer under every robotics platform.
robotics_scope: Indirect but structural: targets the semiconductor-manufacturing-equipment supply chain that produces the compute (including robot-compute chips like D-Robotics' Sunrise line) every robotics platform depends on, rather than robots themselves.

title: 2026 National Security Science and Technology Strategy
summary: The 2026 NSSTS sets four pillars: focused technological competition, resilience, innovation speed, and protection of national-security S&T. It covers federal R&D, nonfederal partnerships, and cooperation with allies.
robotics_scope: Autonomous systems, industrial capacity, research security, test infrastructure, and trusted partners are relevant cross-cutting areas.

title: NSTM-5 — FY2028 Administration R&D Budget Priorities
summary: The FY2028 R&D priority memorandum frames a new golden age of science through federal research investment, mission focus, scientific infrastructure, and private-sector participation.
robotics_scope: Research priorities and infrastructure channels relevant to robotics, autonomous experimentation, manufacturing, and scientific instruments.

title: National Security Presidential Memorandum 11
summary: The memorandum addresses national-security uses of AI and federal coordination. It is a national-security directive, not a general commercial robotics rule.
robotics_scope: Relevant to defense AI and autonomous-system governance within federal national-security missions.

title: White House National AI Legislative Framework
summary: March 2026 legislative recommendations ask Congress to establish a federal AI framework that limits certain state AI laws while preserving specified state roles. It is a recommendation to Congress, not enacted preemption.
robotics_scope: Possible future interaction with state rules for AI models and robot deployment; current state law remains applicable unless displaced by enacted law.

title: Colorado — SB 26-189 Automated Decision-Making Technology Act
summary: Colorado repealed and reenacted its high-risk AI consumer-protection provisions in 2026. The new ADMT Act governs automated technology that materially influences consequential decisions and takes effect January 1, 2027. The Attorney General is preparing rules; it is not a general robot-operation code.
robotics_scope: Potential effect only where a robot-enabled system materially influences a covered consequential decision; ordinary physical robot operation is not automatically in scope.

title: Philadelphia — Bill 260526, autonomous delivery unit fees and registration
summary: The proposed ordinance would register some delivery workers and autonomous delivery units and impose a $1,000 fee per sidewalk delivery by an autonomous unit. The city legislative record lists it in committee as of September 2026; the fee is not in effect.
robotics_scope: Proposed local rules and fee for sidewalk delivery robots.

title: NIST MEP center awards for advanced manufacturing adoption
sponsor: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST announced more than $30 million in first-year awards for 12 MEP centers in 11 states and Puerto Rico. Cooperative agreements target small and medium-sized manufacturers adopting AI, robotics, automation, and additive manufacturing; awardees must secure at least 50% nonfederal matching funds. This is not a robotics-only grant to individual startups.
robotics_scope: Technical assistance and adoption metrics for small and medium-sized manufacturers.
